bookInfo.name: New History of the Five Dynasties

title.zh: 卷十八 漢家人傳第六:
title.en: Volume 18: The Later Han Imperial Family
title.raw: 卷十八 漢家人傳第六: Volume 18: The Later Han Imperial Family

sentences.zh: 高祖皇后李氏

translations.literal: Gaozu’s Empress, the Li clan
translations.idiomatic: Empress Li, wife of Gaozu of Later Han

sentences.zh: 帝年少，數與小人郭允明、後贊、李業等遊戲宮中，後數切責之。

translations.literal: When the emperor was young he often played in the palace with petty men Guo Yunming, Hou Zan, Li Ye, and others; the empress repeatedly rebuked him sternly.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth the emperor often caroused in the palace with Guo Yunming, Hou Zan, Li Ye, and other low companions; the empress scolded him again and again.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「國家之事，外有朝廷，非太后所宜言也。

translations.literal: The emperor said: “State affairs are handled outside, with the court—this is not what the empress dowager should speak of.
translations.idiomatic: He said: “Government belongs to the court outside—the empress dowager should not meddle.

sentences.zh: 」太常卿張昭聞之，上疏諫帝，請：「親近師傅，延問正人，以開聰明。

translations.literal: ” The Minister of Ceremonies Zhang Zhao heard of it and memorialized to admonish the emperor, asking that he “draw near teachers, extend inquiry to upright men, and open his intelligence.
translations.idiomatic: ” Minister of Ceremonies Zhang Zhao heard and urged him to keep close to tutors, seek wise counsel, and sharpen his mind.

sentences.zh: 」帝益不省。

translations.literal: ” The emperor was even less reflective.
translations.idiomatic: ” The emperor paid even less heed.

sentences.zh: 其後，帝卒與允明等謀議，遂至於亡。

translations.literal: Later the emperor at last plotted with Yunming and the others, and came to ruin.
translations.idiomatic: In time he plotted with Yunming and the rest—and brought ruin on himself.

sentences.zh: 初，帝與允明等謀誅楊邠、史弘肇等，議已定，入白太后。

translations.literal: At first, when the emperor and Yunming and the others plotted to execute Yang Bin, Shi Hongzhao, and the rest, and the plan was settled, he entered to tell the empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: When he and Yunming had settled on killing Yang Bin, Shi Hongzhao, and the others, he told the empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 太后曰：「此大事也，當與宰相議之。

translations.literal: The empress dowager said: “This is a great affair—it should be discussed with the chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: She said: “This is grave—it must go to the chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 」李業從旁對曰：「先皇帝平生言，朝廷大事，勿問書生。

translations.literal: ” Li Ye answered from the side: “The late emperor always said that in great court affairs one must not ask scholars.
translations.idiomatic: ” Li Ye cut in: “The late emperor always said never to ask scholars about great affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 」太后深以為不可，帝拂衣而去，曰：「何必謀於閨門！

translations.literal: ” The empress dowager deeply thought this wrong; the emperor shook out his robes and left, saying: “Why must we plot within the women’s quarters!
translations.idiomatic: ” She strongly objected; he flung off and left, saying: “Must we take counsel only from the inner quarters!

sentences.zh: 」邠等死，周太祖起兵向京師，慕容彥超敗於劉子陂，帝欲出自臨兵，太后止之曰：「郭威本吾家人，非其危疑，何肯至此！

translations.literal: ” When Bin and the others were dead, Taizu of Zhou raised troops toward the capital; Murong Yanchao was defeated at Liuzipo; the emperor wished to go out in person to command the army; the empress dowager stopped him, saying: “Guo Wei was originally one of our household—had he not been driven to doubt, how would he have come to this!
translations.idiomatic: ” After their deaths, Guo Wei marched on the capital; Yanchao fell at Liuzipo; the emperor meant to take the field himself; the dowager stopped him: “Guo Wei was always of our house—only fear and suspicion drove him here!

sentences.zh: 今若按兵無動，以詔諭威，威必有說，則君臣之際，庶幾尚全。

translations.literal: Now if you hold the army still and do not move, and with an edict explain matters to Wei, Wei will surely have something to say—then between lord and minister perhaps something may still be preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Hold your troops, send him an edict of explanation—he will answer, and lord and minister may yet be whole.

sentences.zh: 」帝不從以出，遂及於難。

translations.literal: ” The emperor would not listen and went out, and met disaster.
translations.idiomatic: ” He refused and went out—and met disaster.

sentences.zh: 周太祖入京師，舉事皆稱太后誥。

translations.literal: When Taizu of Zhou entered the capital, in all affairs he invoked the empress dowager’s edicts.
translations.idiomatic: When Guo Wei entered the capital, he acted in the dowager’s name.

sentences.zh: 已而議立湘陰公赟為天子，赟未至，太祖乃請太后臨朝。

translations.literal: Soon they deliberated enthroning the Duke of Xiangyin, Yun, as Son of Heaven; before Yun arrived, Taizu asked the empress dowager to hold court.
translations.idiomatic: They meant to make the Duke of Xiangyin, Yun, emperor; before he arrived, Guo Wei had the dowager hold court.

sentences.zh: 已而太祖出征契丹，軍士擁之以還。

translations.literal: Soon Taizu campaigned against the Khitan; the soldiers forced him back.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wei marched against the Khitan; the army forced him back.

sentences.zh: 太祖請事太后為母，太后誥曰：「侍中功烈崇高，德聲昭著，剪除禍亂，安定邦家，謳歌有歸，歷數攸屬，所以軍民推戴，億兆同歡。

translations.literal: Taizu asked to treat the empress dowager as his mother; the dowager’s edict said: “The attendant-in-chief’s merit is lofty, his virtue renowned; he has cut away calamity and settled the realm; songs of praise have a target, the mandate has found its seat—therefore the army and people have pushed him forward, the millions rejoice together.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to honor her as mother; her edict read: “The attendant-in-chief’s merit towers, his virtue shines; he has ended chaos and steadied the realm—the army and people have chosen him, and all rejoice.

sentences.zh: 老身未終殘年，屬此多難，唯以衰朽，托於始終。

translations.literal: I have not finished my declining years, yet meet such many troubles; only in my decay do I entrust myself to the end.
translations.idiomatic: I have not outlived my years, yet meet such troubles; in my weakness I trust myself to the end.

sentences.zh: 載省來箋，如母見待，感認深意，涕泗橫流。

translations.literal: Reading your letter, you treat me as a mother—I feel the deep meaning and my tears stream.
translations.idiomatic: Your letter treats me as a mother—I am moved to tears.

sentences.zh: 」於是迂後於太平宮，上尊號曰昭聖皇太后。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon she was moved to the Taiping Palace and honored as Empress Dowager Zhaosheng.
translations.idiomatic: ” She was moved to Taiping Palace and titled Empress Dowager Zhaosheng.

sentences.zh: 顯德元年春崩。

translations.literal: In spring of the first year of Xiande she died.
translations.idiomatic: She died in spring of Xiande 1.

sentences.zh: 高祖弟子侄

translations.literal: Gaozu’s younger brothers and nephews
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu’s younger brothers and nephews

sentences.zh: 高祖二弟三子：弟曰崇、曰信，子曰承訓、承祐、承勛。

translations.literal: Gaozu had two younger brothers and three sons: the brothers Chong and Xin; the sons Chengxun, Chengyou, and Chenghsun.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu had two brothers—Chong and Xin—and three sons: Chengxun, Chengyou, and Chenghsun.

sentences.zh: 崇子曰赟，高祖愛之，以為己子。

translations.literal: Chong’s son Yun—Gaozu loved him and took him as his own son.
translations.idiomatic: Chong’s son Yun was loved by Gaozu and adopted as his son.

sentences.zh: 乾祐元年，拜赟徐州節度使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianyou, Yun was made military governor of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianyou 1, Yun became military governor of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 承訓早卒，追封魏王。

translations.literal: Chengxun died young and was posthumously created Prince of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxun died young and was posthumously made Prince of Wei.

sentences.zh: 承祐次立，是謂隱帝。

translations.literal: Chengyou succeeded next and is called the Hidden Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Chengyou succeeded next—the Hidden Emperor.

sentences.zh: 承勛為開封尹。

translations.literal: Chenghsun was metropolitan governor of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Chenghsun was governor of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 周太祖已敗漢兵於北郊，隱帝遇弒。

translations.literal: Taizu of Zhou had already defeated Han troops at the northern suburb; the Hidden Emperor was assassinated.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wei had beaten Han at the northern suburb; the Hidden Emperor was killed.

sentences.zh: 太祖入京師，以謂漢大臣必相推戴，及見宰相馮道等，道殊無意，太祖不得已，見道猶下拜，道受太祖拜如平時，徐勞之曰：「公行良苦！

translations.literal: When Taizu entered the capital he thought Han ministers would surely push him forward; when he saw chief minister Feng Dao and the others, Dao showed no intent; Taizu had no choice; seeing Dao he still bowed; Dao received the bow as in ordinary times and slowly comforted him: “Your journey was hard!
translations.idiomatic: Entering the capital, Guo Wei expected Han ministers to acclaim him; Feng Dao showed no sign; forced, Guo Wei still bowed; Dao accepted the bow as usual and said slowly: “A hard road!

sentences.zh: 」太祖意色皆沮，以謂漢大臣未有推立己意，又難於自立，因白漢太后擇立漢嗣。

translations.literal: ” Taizu’s expression and color were both dejected; he thought Han ministers had no intent to raise him; it was hard to raise himself; he therefore told Han’s empress dowager to choose a Han heir.
translations.idiomatic: ” Guo Wei’s face fell; no Han minister meant to make him emperor; he asked the dowager to choose a Han heir.

sentences.zh: 而宗室河東節度使崇等在者四人，乃為太后誥曰：「河東節度使崇，許州節度使信，皆高祖之弟，徐州節度使赟，開封尹承勛，皆高祖之子，文武百辟，其擇嗣君以承天統。

translations.literal: Among the imperial clan, Chong of Hedong and the others, four were present; an edict was issued for the dowager: “Chong, military governor of Hedong, and Xin, military governor of Xu—both Gaozu’s younger brothers; Yun, military governor of Xuzhou, and Chenghsun, metropolitan governor of Kaifeng—both Gaozu’s sons: civil and military officials, choose an heir to receive Heaven’s succession.
translations.idiomatic: Four of the Liu clan remained; the dowager’s edict named Chong of Hedong, Xin of Xu, Yun of Xuzhou, and Chenghsun of Kaifeng—brothers and sons of Gaozu—and bade the court choose an heir.

sentences.zh: 」於是周太祖與王峻入見太后，言：「開封尹承勛，高祖皇帝之子，宜立。

translations.literal: Thereupon Taizu of Zhou and Wang Jun entered to see the empress dowager, saying: “Chenghsun, Kaifeng metropolitan governor, is Gaozu’s son—he should be enthroned.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wei and Wang Jun told the dowager: “Chenghsun, Gaozu’s son, should reign.

sentences.zh: 」太后以承勛久病，不任為嗣。

translations.literal: ” The empress dowager said Chenghsun had long been ill and could not bear the succession.
translations.idiomatic: ” She said Chenghsun was too ill.

sentences.zh: 太祖與群臣請見承勛視起居，太后命以臥榻舁承勛出見群臣，群臣視之信然，乃共奏曰：「徐州節度使赟，高祖愛之，以為子，宜立為嗣。

translations.literal: Taizu and the ministers asked to see Chenghsun to observe his rising and resting; the empress dowager ordered him carried out on a couch to meet the ministers; the ministers saw it was true; they jointly memorialized: “Yun, military governor of Xuzhou, whom Gaozu loved and made his son, should be enthroned as heir.
translations.idiomatic: They asked to see Chenghsun; he was borne out on a couch; seeing him truly ill, they memorialized for Yun, whom Gaozu had adopted.

sentences.zh: 」乃遣太師馮道率群臣迎赟。

translations.literal: ” Grand Preceptor Feng Dao then led the ministers to welcome Yun.
translations.idiomatic: ” Feng Dao led the ministers to welcome Yun.

sentences.zh: 道揣周太祖意不在赟，謂太祖曰：「公此舉由衷乎？

translations.literal: Dao gauged that Taizu of Zhou’s intent was not on Yun and said to Taizu: “Is this action from the heart?
translations.idiomatic: Dao sensed Guo Wei did not mean to enthrone Yun and asked: “Do you mean this sincerely?

sentences.zh: 」太祖指天為誓。

translations.literal: ” Taizu pointed to Heaven and swore.
translations.idiomatic: ” Guo Wei swore to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 道既行，謂人曰：「吾平生不為謬語人，今謬語矣！

translations.literal: ” After Dao departed he told others: “All my life I have not spoken falsely to people—today I have spoken falsely!
translations.idiomatic: ” Leaving, he said: “I have never lied to anyone—today I lied!

sentences.zh: 」道見赟，傳太后意召之。

translations.literal: ” When Dao saw Yun he conveyed the empress dowager’s intent to summon him.
translations.idiomatic: ” He told Yun the dowager summoned him.

sentences.zh: 赟行至宋州，太祖自澶州為兵士擁還京師，王峻慮赟左右生變，遣侍衛馬軍指揮使郭崇以兵七百騎衛赟。

translations.literal: As Yun traveled to Songzhou, Taizu from Dazhou was forced back to the capital by soldiers; Wang Jun feared Yun’s attendants might stir trouble and sent palace guard horse commander Guo Chong with seven hundred cavalry to escort Yun.
translations.idiomatic: At Songzhou, Guo Wei was forced back from Dazhou; Wang Jun sent Guo Chong with seven hundred horse to guard Yun.

sentences.zh: 崇至宋州，赟登樓問崇所以來之意，崇曰：「澶州軍變，懼未察之，遣崇護衛，非惡意也。

translations.literal: When Chong reached Songzhou, Yun ascended a tower and asked Chong’s purpose; Chong said: “There was mutiny at Dazhou; fearing matters were unclear, he was sent to guard—no ill intent.
translations.idiomatic: Chong came; Yun asked why; Chong said Dazhou had mutinied and he came to protect him, not harm him.

sentences.zh: 」赟召崇，崇不敢進，馮道出與崇語，崇乃登樓見赟，已而奪赟部下兵。

translations.literal: ” Yun summoned Chong; Chong dared not enter; Feng Dao went out to speak with Chong; Chong then ascended the tower and saw Yun; before long he seized Yun’s followers’ troops.
translations.idiomatic: ” Yun called him up; Chong hesitated until Feng Dao spoke with him; then he entered—and disarmed Yun’s men.

sentences.zh: 太祖以書召道先歸，留其副趙上交、王度奉赟入朝太后。

translations.literal: Taizu by letter summoned Dao to return first and left his deputies Zhao Shangjiao and Wang Du to escort Yun into court to the empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wei recalled Dao first and left Zhao Shangjiao and Wang Du to bring Yun to court.

sentences.zh: 道乃先還，赟謂道曰：「寡人此來，所恃者以公三十年舊相，是以不疑。

translations.literal: Dao returned first; Yun said to Dao: “In coming here I relied on you as my minister of thirty years—therefore I did not doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Dao left; Yun said: “I trusted you as minister of thirty years—that is why I came.

sentences.zh: 」道默然。

translations.literal: ” Dao was silent.
translations.idiomatic: ” Dao said nothing.

sentences.zh: 赟客將賈正等數目道，欲圖之。

translations.literal: Yun’s guest officer Jia Zheng and several others eyed Dao, intending to plot against him.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Zheng and others watched Dao, plotting.

sentences.zh: 赟曰：「勿草草，事豈出於公邪！

translations.literal: Yun said: “Do not be rash—could the affair lie outside the minister!
translations.idiomatic: Yun said: “Do not be hasty—surely the minister is not behind this!

sentences.zh: 」道已去，郭崇幽赟於外館，殺賈正及判官董裔、牙內都虞候劉福、孔目官夏昭度等。

translations.literal: ” After Dao was gone, Guo Chong confined Yun in an outer lodge and killed Jia Zheng, registrar Dong Yi, inner guard chief adjutant Liu Fu, clerk Xia Zhaodu, and others.
translations.idiomatic: ” Dao gone, Chong imprisoned Yun and killed Jia Zheng, Dong Yi, Liu Fu, Xia Zhaodu, and others.

sentences.zh: 太祖已監國，太后乃下誥曰：「此者樞密使郭威，誌安宗社，議立長君，以徐州節度使赟高祖近親，立為漢嗣，乃自藩鎮召赴京師。

translations.literal: Taizu was already regent; the empress dowager then issued an edict: “Here the commissioner Guo Wei, intent on settling the altars, deliberated enthroning the elder lord; because Yun, military governor of Xuzhou, was Gaozu’s close kin, he was made Han heir and summoned from his command to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: As regent, the dowager issued an edict: Guo Wei had meant to enthrone an elder lord; Yun, Gaozu’s kin, was chosen and summoned from Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 雖誥命已行，而軍情不附，天道在北，人心靡東。

translations.literal: Though the decree had gone forth, the army’s heart did not adhere; Heaven’s way lay in the north, men’s hearts not in the east.
translations.idiomatic: The decree went out, but the army would not follow; Heaven favored the north, not the east.

sentences.zh: 適當改卜之初，俾膺分土之命，赟可降授開府儀同三司，檢校太師、上柱國，封湘陰公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of changing the choice, let him receive a fief’s command: Yun may be demoted to Kaifu Yitong Sansi, acting Grand Preceptor, supreme pillar of state, and enfeoffed Duke of Xiangyin.
translations.idiomatic: Yun was demoted to Kaifu Yitong Sansi, acting Grand Preceptor, supreme pillar of state, and made Duke of Xiangyin.

sentences.zh: 」赟以幽死。

translations.literal: ” Yun died under confinement.
translations.idiomatic: ” Yun died imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 初，赟自徐州入也，以都押衙鞏庭美、教練使楊溫守徐州。

translations.literal: At first, when Yun came from Xuzhou, he left chief adjutant Gong Tingmei and drill officer Yang Wen to hold Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving Xuzhou, Yun had Gong Tingmei and Yang Wen hold the city.

sentences.zh: 庭美等聞赟不得立，乃閉城拒命。

translations.literal: When Tingmei and the others heard Yun could not be enthroned, they closed the city and defied orders.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing Yun would not reign, they shut the city and resisted.

sentences.zh: 太祖拜王彥超徐州節度使，下詔諭庭美等許以刺史，並詔赟赦庭美等。

translations.literal: Taizu made Wang Yanchao military governor of Xuzhou, issued edicts telling Tingmei and the others they would be made prefects, and also edicts in Yun’s name pardoning Tingmei and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wei made Wang Yanchao governor and promised Tingmei and Wen prefectures, even pardons in Yun’s name.

sentences.zh: 廣順元年三月，彥超克徐州，庭美等皆見殺。

translations.literal: In the third month of the first year of Guangshun, Yanchao took Xuzhou; Tingmei and the others were all killed.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Guangshun 1, Yanchao took Xuzhou and killed them.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 予既悲湘陰公赟之事，又嘉庭美、楊溫之所為。

translations.literal: I grieve the affair of the Duke of Xiangyin, Yun, and also praise what Tingmei and Yang Wen did.
translations.idiomatic: I mourn Duke of Xiangyin Yun, and praise Tingmei and Yang Wen.

sentences.zh: 赟於漢非嫡長，特以周氏移國，畏天下而難之，故假赟以伺間爾。

translations.literal: Yun was not Han’s eldest son by the principal wife; only because the Zhou house changed the dynasty, fearing the realm, they made difficulty and therefore used Yun to watch for an opening.
translations.idiomatic: Yun was not Han’s heir; the Zhou change made him a pawn while they waited their chance.

sentences.zh: 當是之時，天下皆知赟之必不立也，然庭美、溫之區區為赟守孤城以死，其始終之跡，何愧於死節之士哉！

translations.literal: At that time all under Heaven knew Yun would surely not be enthroned; yet Tingmei and Wen, in their small way, held a lone city for Yun unto death—their course from start to end: how do they shame men who died for principle!
translations.idiomatic: Everyone knew Yun would never reign; yet Tingmei and Wen held one city for him unto death—what loyal death could shame them?

sentences.zh: 然予考於實錄，二人之死狀不明。

translations.literal: Yet when I examine the true record, how the two men died is unclear.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the true record does not say how they died.

sentences.zh: 夫二人之事，固知其無所成，其所重者死爾，然史氏不著，不知其何以死也。

translations.literal: In the affair of the two men, it is known they could not succeed; what they valued was death itself—yet the historians do not record it, and one does not know how they died.
translations.idiomatic: They knew they could not win; they sought death—but the historians leave it blank.

sentences.zh: 當王彥超之攻徐州也，周嘗遣人招庭美等，予得其詔書四，皆言庭美等嘗已送款於周，後懼罪而復叛，然庭美等款狀亦不見，是皆不可知也。

translations.literal: When Wang Yanchao attacked Xuzhou, Zhou once sent men to summon Tingmei and the others; I obtained four of their edicts, all saying Tingmei and the others had already submitted to Zhou and later, fearing guilt, rebelled again—yet their submission is also not seen; all is unknowable.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanchao besieged Xuzhou, Zhou summoned them; I have four edicts claiming they had submitted then rebelled from fear—but no submission survives; nothing is certain.

sentences.zh: 夫史之闕文，要不慎哉。

translations.literal: The gaps in history must be treated with caution!
translations.idiomatic: Gaps in history demand caution!

sentences.zh: 其疑以傳疑，則信者信矣。

translations.literal: Where doubt passes on doubt, what is sure remains sure.
translations.idiomatic: Pass doubt as doubt, and certainty stays certain.

sentences.zh: 予固嘉二人之忠而悲其志，然不得列於死節之士者，惜哉！

translations.literal: I praise the two men’s loyalty and grieve their aim, yet regret they cannot be listed among those who died for principle!
translations.idiomatic: I honor their loyalty and mourn their aim—yet they cannot stand among those who died for principle.

sentences.zh: 高祖從弟信

translations.literal: Gaozu’s younger cousin Xin
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu’s younger cousin Xin
